key_insight: Multiwavelength photoluminescence non-destructively reveals depth-dependent UV damage in perovskite solar cells, with degradation concentrated near the buried hole-transport-layer interface.
engineering_relevance: Depth-sensitive optical screening can guide interface design, including 3-mercaptopropyltrimethoxysilane modification that improves UV stability.
method: Use wavelength-dependent absorption to probe different depths.
Combine wide-field PL imaging, time-resolved PL and ideality-factor measurements.
Compare perovskite films and p-i-n devices with different ITO modifiers under UV soaking.
evidence_signal: Nondestructive measurements localized preferential interface degradation, consistent with destructive tests, and showed reduced UV damage after interface modification.
watch_item: The abstract reports no quantitative stability gains or validation under broader aging conditions beyond UV soaking.
paper_title: Multiwavelength Photoluminescence as a Non-destructive Probe of Depth-Dependent UV Damage in Perovskite Semiconductors
